name: Ija-Zuba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog entry retired (split into Koro Nulu/Koro Zuba); no descriptive works listed

sources.citation: Yusuf, Stephen Kunle. 2011. Aspects of Ija-Koro phonology. B.A. long essay, University of Ilorin (07/15CB107).
sources.note: Only a generic textbook list of suprasegmentals ('tones, intonation, stress, length'); ch.4: register tones H M L, tone phonemic. Identity doubtful: lexicon matches Jili/Tanjijili [uji] rather than the Koro Nulu list in Decker et al. 2021 (per the koro1323 audit).

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Samuel Eju, Adedamola Aregbesola, Fittokka Gobak, Andrew Lewinan, Luther Hon & Thelma Araokanmi. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Koro Nulu [vkn] and Koro Zuba [vkz], formerly Ija-Zuba [vki], Languages of Central Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-051. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3.2-8.3.3 give only consonant/vowel inventories and sound correspondences for Koro Nulu, Koro Zuba, Dibo; Appendix D p.35: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis done of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.'

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-032 (A. Aregbesola, SIL Nigeria): split Ija-Zuba [vki] into Koro Nulu [vkn] and Koro Zuba [vkz] (adopted 2021-01-15); with the two New Code Request forms.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative document (names, locations, populations, 7% lexical similarity between Koro Nulu and Koro Zuba, Koro Zuba closest to Dibo [dio] at 30-36%).

sources.citation: Adebayo, Funke Christiana. 2011. Aspects of question formation in Ija-Koro. B.A. long essay, University of Ilorin (07/15CB012).
sources.note: Generic suprasegmental list only ('intonation, stress, length'); says tone changes word meaning in Ija-Koro. Same doubtful (Jili-like) identity as Yusuf 2011. No stress rule.

sources.citation: Bakare, Bimbo Mary. 2011. Aspects of Koro morphology. B.A. long essay, Dept. of Linguistics and Nigerian Languages, University of Ilorin. [Glottolog 547181; language of Ija-Koro, Tafa LGA = Koro Nulu]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: No stress statement. Sec. 2.6-2.7 'Tone Patterns': 'Koro has three level tones known as low tone..., a high tone..., and mid tone', plus a falling contour tone; syllable structure CV, CVV, VCV.

sources.citation: Obatoye, Julianah Folasade. 2011. The Koro-Ija noun phrase. B.A. long essay, University of Ilorin. [Glottolog 319684; Ija-Koro village, Tafa LGA = Koro Nulu]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: No stress statement. Sec. 2.1.5 'Tone System in Koro-Ija Language': 'Koro a Niger-Congo language is tonal. The language attests to register tones' (High, Low, Mid); 2.1.6 lexical/grammatical functions of tone.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014. The Jijili (Koro) language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Ms. circulated at rogerblench.info (Plateau/South/Jijili).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not fetched sources
sources.note: Cited by the ISO change request; Blench's Plateau sketches usually include a short tone/phonology note; would confirm whether anything phonological was ever recorded for Koro Ija/Koro Zuba (probably mention only).

sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Benard Abraham. 2022. Sociolinguistic Profile of the Kami [kmi] Language of Niger State, Nigeria with Additional Observations on Nupe Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-021. Dallas: SIL International. 57 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not fetched sources
sources.note: Only other professional publication touching Koro Zuba (pp.17-18, Nupoid affiliation); may contain phonological notes on Koro Zuba, though as a survey report a stress statement is unlikely.

sources.citation: Sterk, Jan P. 1977. Elements of Gade Grammar. PhD dissertation, University of Wisconsin-Madison (word lists pp. 252-264 include a Koro list from the Zuba area).
